column1: # Word lists the language verdict reads. One per line, tab separated.
#   code       language tag; becomes <code>.txt in the cache and shows up in the verdict
#   bron       a URL, or SYSTEM to copy /usr/share/dict/words
#   vorm       plain = one word per line | freq = "word count" per line, count stripped
#   licentie   what the source allows, so attribution is not guesswork
#   naam       what to call it in output
# Adding a language is one line. A file dropped into the cache by hand is picked up too,
# as long as it is <code>.txt: the verdict reads the cache, not this file.
# English is deliberately a FREQUENCY list, not a dictionary. Webster's full list (which is
# what /usr/share/dict/words holds) contains merk, wis, wissel and knop as obscure entries,
# so "not in English" was true of almost nothing and the verdict collapsed. The 50k most
# common words answer the question actually being asked: would an English speaker use this.
